title: How do we tile any grid with an even number of rows?
description: A grid with m rows and n columns, where m and n are both even. Each column has an even number of squares, so upright tiles fill it, and all the columns together cover the grid. Keeko's doubt, that this works only for square grids, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: a column with an even number of squares is filled by upright tiles, and the plan works column after column. Watch for students who think the plan needs the same number of rows and columns.

source: Is an m × n grid tileable with 2 × 1 tiles if both m and n a
video_script.why: The child finds a plan that tiles every grid whose sides are both even.
video_script.substitution: A column of m squares, with m even, takes m divided by two vertical tiles.
video_script.anchor: A grid of unit squares with m rows and n columns, where m and n are both even, and a tile that covers 2 squares.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the plan works only for square grids, with equal rows and columns. But the example has six rows and four columns, and it worked. Only the length of a column matters.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, cover each column with vertical tiles.

final_answer.value: Yes: cover each column with vertical tiles
final_answer.spoken: yes, cover each column with vertical tiles

hold_back: cover each column with vertical tiles
maths_rules: Each column has m squares, and m is even.
Cover each column with m ÷ 2 vertical tiles.
Every column is covered, so the whole grid is covered with no gaps or overlaps.
Example: a 6 × 4 grid uses 3 vertical tiles in each of 4 columns, 12 tiles in all.
Slip: the plan needs an even column length, not equal rows and columns.
video_script.design: One general grid, then one example, six rows and four columns. A column is filled by upright tiles and the plan repeats across the grid. The slip is the idea that only a square grid works.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the plan works only for square grids, with equal rows and columns.
